newsitem.title: USA: W. House backs recovery of past local phone costs.
newsitem.headline: W. House backs recovery of past local phone costs.

text.p: The Clinton administration on Monday said local telephone companies should be allowed to recover some of the historic costs of maintaining and upgrading their local networks.
The view lends support to the Baby Bells' position in the heated debate over how to reduce the $20 billion they collect each year for handling long-distance calls on their local networks.

The Federal Communications Commission currently is studying how to reform the practice of charging those so-called access charges. The Bells have advocated that they should be allowed to recover historic costs.
The administration, in its annual Economic Report of the President, said "recovery of costs legitimately incurred pursuant to regulatory obligations would be warranted."
Still, it added that "such recovery should be limited ... to investment expenses not already recovered through past earnings."
Long-distance carriers have complained that current access charges are inflated and that the Bells are using the suprlus to pad their profits.

But the local companies say long-distance carriers have underestimated the cost of maintaining and upgrading the local networks and base their assertions on theoretical cost models that do not always reflect reality.
